snip.t: | Radioactive iodine uptake (RAIU) scan | Etiology (diffuse vs nodular) | Uniform high uptake → Graves’; patchy → toxic multinodular; low uptake → thyroiditis |

Radioactive iodine uptake scan (technetium or I-131): diffusely increased uptake in Graves'; patchy ("hot and cold") uptake in multinodular goitre; a single hot nodule with a suppressed rest of the gland in a toxic adenoma; low uptake in thyroiditis.

snip.t: The treatment of patients exposed to 131I involves using potassium iodide to block radioactive iodine uptake, monitoring thyroid function, administering thyroid hormone replacement if hypothyroidism develops, and monitoring for radiation-induced thyroid cancer.

qs.q: A patient presents with thyrotoxicosis symptoms, elevated free T4, and suppressed TSH, but has a small thyroid gland, very low serum thyroglobulin, and suppressed radioactive iodine uptake. What condition does this profile suggest?
o: Thyrotoxicosis factitia caused by exogenous hormone intake
Graves disease with primary autoimmune thyroid activation
Toxic multinodular goiter producing autonomous secretion
TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma driving excessive hormones
qs.e: Thyrotoxicosis factitia is caused by exogenous thyroid hormone ingestion, leading to a small gland, low thyroglobulin, and suppressed radioactive iodine uptake. Graves disease, by contrast, shows an enlarged gland and elevated radioactive iodine uptake.
